text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: This is a non-review research article presenting a spatially-explicit state-and-transition simulation model, LUCAS, developed and applied at the national scale for the conterminous U.S. The primary focus is on land use and land cover (LULC) prediction/simulation and its impact on carbon dynamics. The paper describes the integration of multiple national datasets, harmonization methods, spatial multipliers, and forest age data to initialize the model. It implements multiple future scenarios (including IPCC-SRES A1B) with quantitative spatial outputs of LULC projections over a 100-year period and includes verification and sensitivity analyses demonstrating quantitative model accuracy and uncertainty. The study area and model inputs/outputs are explicitly national scale with regional subsets used for illustration. The modeling approach is spatially explicit with mapped outputs and quantitative evaluation of transition probabilities and spatial allocation. The paper does not meet any exclusion criteria such as local/regional-only focus, lack of LULC prediction, or absence of multiple scenarios. Therefore, it fully meets all core inclusion criteria for national-scale, spatially explicit, multi-scenario LULC prediction research.)
